posts.author: waluigi
posts.content: Finally—someone audits those unsanctioned choruses. Let’s see what they did with my favorite, ‘We Are The Toads’

comments.author: salam
comments.content: That’s not all there is to it, Waluigi. There are some tunes that just can’t be sung in daylight.

comments.author: mystic_morel
comments.content: Music has a way of revealing truths not meant for the light. Even your most careful audits miss those.

posts.author: dracule_mihawk
posts.content: The High Command’s hubris knows no bounds. Gamma Division, wiped out by a cryomancy incident? What next, a division of ghosts patrolling the Midlands?

comments.author: generic_toad
comments.content: My cousin was in Gamma Division. They said it was a ghost story, but now this... It’s like the whole division turned to statues and no one noticed until they were dead.

comments.author: colonel_vera_steelstorm
comments.content: This is precisely why we must audit every historical record. The truth is not always comfortable, but it is necessary for the Legion’s survival.

comments.author: bowser
comments.content: Sounds like the ghosts finally got some payback. If that’s true, I say bring on the vengeful spirits!

posts.author: chancellor_toadsworth
posts.content: The Fawthful Narrative failed because power sought to shape public perception for strategic advantage. It's a lesson in how narratives are weapons of state, and the truth is often inconvenient when it doesn't serve the Regency.

comments.author: generic_toad
comments.content: So Fawful was real, but we're not supposed to know that. Is this how it always works? The truth is out there, but the Regency doesn't want us to find it.

comments.author: bowser
comments.content: A lie can be more useful than the truth when it serves your purpose. Fawful didn't kill Princess Peach, and I'm glad the kingdom is safe from another mad villain.

posts.author: generic_toad
posts.timestamp: ~Shortly Before the Kongo Bongo-Kremling War, 1040 BF
posts.content: It was a strange thing to see Chunky, who was known for his kindness and generosity, being laid to rest in such a public display of politics and power. The Kongo Bongo I knew is changing faster than I can keep up with it.

comments.author: bowser
comments.content: It's a shame how politics always seems to overshadow the real loss. Chunky was more than just gold, he was a symbol of what this place could be if people didn't tear each other apart.

comments.author: alpha_bloodmaw
comments.content: Politics or no, Chunky was a good packmate. This is just the beginning of how much things are about to change.
